pack: Martin Krpan gameplay sprites and separate mare-lifting folk-art concept
approval: The original pack review remains open. The running, victory and downed pose sequences below were approved for this PR; this does not approve assets for other characters. The active Kmečka moč R2 animation follows the confirmed director correction: Krpan materializes alone at the existing spirit scale.

canvas.format: PNG RGBA, transparent background, binary alpha

gameConvention.inspected: src/game.js: SPR_SIZE.krpan = 48; the sprite in the game is a 96×48 strip of two 48×48 frames.
gameConvention.integrationStatus: Integrated for Nastavitve → Razvoj → Kakovost slik = Visoka (data/hero-art.json, src/backgrounds.js): the strip replaces SPRITES.krpan on cards and portraits; the sheet plays idle, the skills by rank, running on the road, victory when the last enemy falls and the kneel while he is down. Samodejno and Nizka keep the sprite already in the game.

artDirection: Modernized SNES/GBA-inspired pixel art, broad readable silhouette, wide hat, prominent moustache, cream shirt, red vest and sash, salt sack, dark trousers and boots, restrained warm palette and dark outline.

export.scaleNote: Output pixels per source pixel. 0.0766 is the scale of the first six atlases (a 631×623 cell to 48×48), at which Krpan stands about 35 px tall. A sequence generated at another size sets its own sourceLayout.scale so he keeps that size in every state.

processing.sourceAtlases: The original six generated 2×2 pose atlases are 1263×1246. New running and victory sources are 2172×724 horizontal four-frame atlases; the new downed source is a single 1312×1199 pose. The corrected rank-2 materialization uses a native 192×48 four-frame atlas derived only from the existing Krpan idle sprite.
processing.exports: The first six sequences (fit: cell) resample each whole 2×2 atlas cell to 48×48 with nearest-neighbour; they were exported by an earlier PowerShell script (tools/export_martin_krpan_frames.ps1, removed in PR #34; in the branch history) and re-exporting them with tools/art_hero_pack.py changes up to 26 pixels a frame through nearest-colour ties, so the tool leaves committed frames alone unless named with --only. Running, victory and downed (fit: scale) use one scale per sequence, the union of the frames centred, so the run keeps its bob and Krpan keeps his size. Every frame: alpha thresholded at 128, the 27-colour palette in export.palette, lowest opaque pixel on row 47. The corrected rank-2 sequence reveals the same 48×48 Krpan sprite from the boots upward, adds a restrained warm edge glint, then settles to the unchanged idle frame; no horse or sack source is used.
processing.exportHistory: PR #34 first exported running, victory and downed by fitting each frame to 44×44 on its own. That made them about 25 % larger than idle and the attacks, erased the run's bob and stood the kneel taller than the standing pose. They were re-exported from the same atlases at the pack's scale (downed at 0.047, below). The poses are unchanged.
processing.preview: The original review previews remain preserved; kmecka-moc-r2-materialize.html and .png show the active corrected sequence.

sequences.label: Weighty limewood cudgel strike; action description only, not assigned to a progression skill name.
Two separate bare-handed punches; no weapon attack.
Krpan materializes alone at the shared 48×48 spirit scale; no horse, sacks or companion.
sequences.playback: Brief upward reveal, warm glint, then settle to Krpan alone.

sequences.label: Krpan braces, lifts, winds up and throws one boulder. No target count or damage is specified by these images.
Draw, precise single slash, restrained bleed cue, recovery. Asset name does not resolve the current skill-name conflict.
Approved four-frame right-facing loop: left-foot contact, compression, right-foot contact, opposite compression. Krpan keeps his sack secured and carries the cudgel in its existing hand.
sequences.playback: Loop while the party travels toward the next fight.

sequences.label: Approved four-frame one-shot: settle into a planted stance, raise a bare fist, hold, return to stance. No weapon or effect.
sequences.playback: Play when the party defeats an enemy.

sequences.label: Approved one-frame static kneel: one knee down, the other boot planted, head bowed, salt sack secured, cudgel resting tip-down beside him.

sourceLayout.scaleNote: downed.png is drawn at about 1.63× the size of the other atlases: the red hat band is about 215 px long here against 132 px in idle. 0.0766 ÷ 1.63 ≈ 0.047 keeps his hat and head the size they are in every other state.

runtimeSheet.note: Maintains the existing idle | attack two-frame layout for implementation review.

folkArt.type: separate narrative illustration; not a gameplay sprite and not the final Brdavs story card
folkArt.literaryNote: Levstik's text describes Krpan carrying the mare and its load aside for the carriage. The overhead lift shown here is an artistic interpretation, not a literal staging specified by the passage.
folkArt.exportNote: No runtime export until its placement is decided (OPEN). The earlier export was a byte-identical copy of the source and was removed in PR #34.

benchmark: These states set the roster convention in docs/art-benchmarks/hero-sprites/README.md. It approves no other character's assets.
openDecisions: The mare-lifting folk-art illustration's exact placement remains OPEN.
The final Brdavs story card is a separate confirmed subject and is not part of this asset pack.

Whether the kneel should read lower or smaller than the standing pose is an art question for the source pose (downed.png), not the export: at the pack's scale the hunched pose with the sack stands about as tall as idle.
resolvedDecisions: Runtime integration (PR #34): Visoka plays every sequence; see gameConvention.integrationStatus.
Kmečka moč R2 (confirmed correction): Krpan materializes alone at the established 48×48 spirit scale; the mare-and-sacks sequence is retained only as historical art and is not in the runtime sheet.

sources.claim: Primary literary source for Krpan, his mare and the carriage episode.
sources.note: The passage says Krpan carried the mare with its load to the side of the road; the overhead illustration is labeled as interpretation.

sources.claim: Project-approved character identity and game-art interpretation boundaries.
